That changed when Penders, making his first Premier League start, attempted to punch away a corner but inadvertently sent the ball into his own net. The situation became even more difficult when Palmer received a second yellow card, leaving Chelsea with ten players. Tottenham subsequently added another goal through Mathys Tel, securing a 2-0 victory. For Alonso, the match demonstrated how mistakes in crucial moments can undermine a team’s efforts, regardless of the preparation that takes place beforehand. High-pressure situations trigger a range of psychological and physical responses in athletes. The brain must process information in real time, including opponents’ movements, tactical instructions and positioning. Under the effects of adrenaline, some players thrive while others may hesitate or make mistakes. Stress can affect the brain’s decision-making processes, particularly when athletes have little time to assess their options. The same principle of decision-making under pressure can be observed beyond the football pitch. In online poker , for example, players also have to process changing information and make decisions within limited time, although the setting and nature of the decisions are very different. This illustrates how concentration and emotional control can influence decision-making across different activities, without suggesting that their outcomes depend on the same factors. Why mental resilience matters for Chelsea’s squad Chelsea’s current squad combines emerging talent with more experienced footballers, creating an environment in which players must adapt to different expectations and responsibilities. For younger players in particular, the demands of Premier League football can be considerable. Mistakes are analysed immediately, performances are discussed across social media and supporters expect consistent results. Penders’ experience against Tottenham illustrates how difficult these situations can become. Having stepped into the starting line-up following Emiliano Martinez’s injury, the young goalkeeper faced the challenge of performing in a major London derby. His error proved costly, but the ability to recover from such setbacks is an important part of developing as a professional footballer. Mindset plays a significant role in how athletes respond to these experiences. Players who develop mental resilience are often better equipped to block out distractions and maintain their focus. Techniques such as visualization, breathing exercises and simulated match situations can help athletes prepare for moments when emotions run high. For Chelsea, developing that resilience across the squad could prove particularly valuable during a demanding Premier League campaign. The ability to respond positively after conceding a goal, missing an opportunity or making an individual mistake can influence the outcome of closely contested fixtures. Split-second choices can change Chelsea’s matches Football is filled with situations that require instant judgement. A midfielder must decide whether to retain possession or launch a counterattack. A defender has to determine when to press an opponent, while an attacking player may have only seconds to choose between shooting and passing. Chelsea’s performances under Alonso place considerable importance on these decisions. The manager’s tactical approach requires players to understand their positioning, recognise opportunities and respond quickly when possession changes. Even a well-organised system can become vulnerable when individual decisions are poorly timed. Often, success is not simply about technical ability or natural talent. Players must interpret their opponents’ intentions, adapt to changing circumstances and remain aware of tactical instructions throughout a match. Studies in sports psychology explore the importance of psychological preparation in athletic performance. One relevant concept is “decision fatigue”, which describes how sustained mental demands can affect the quality of subsequent choices. During football matches, players repeatedly assess risks, react to opponents and adjust their movements. As physical and mental fatigue increases, maintaining the same level of concentration can become more difficult. This is particularly relevant during the closing stages of matches, when a single defensive mistake or moment of poor judgement can determine the final result. Chelsea’s defeat against Tottenham provided a reminder that maintaining composure is just as important as executing the tactical plan. Alonso faces the challenge of building greater consistency For Xabi Alonso, improving Chelsea’s consistency involves more than refining formations and attacking patterns. The Spanish manager must also help his players develop the confidence and discipline required to perform under pressure. Chelsea’s recent results demonstrate how quickly circumstances can change. The Blues secured a 2-0 away victory against Everton on 17 October, with Pedro Neto scoring twice. A week later, however, the defeat to Tottenham showed how difficult it can be to maintain momentum in the Premier League. Mental preparation is an important complement to physical training at the highest level. Coaching staff can use repetitive drills and match simulations to help players become more comfortable making decisions in demanding situations. Over time, experience also allows footballers to develop stronger “ game intelligence “: the ability to anticipate developments, adapt to changing circumstances and act decisively. This development is especially important for younger Chelsea players who are still gaining experience at senior level. Learning from established teammates and reflecting on difficult matches can help them become better equipped to manage expectations. A strong collective understanding within the squad also matters. Players who trust one another and understand their individual responsibilities are better positioned to respond when a match does not unfold as planned. Stamford Bridge expectations add another layer of pressure The environment surrounding Chelsea can significantly influence how players experience pressure. Stamford Bridge has witnessed major domestic and European successes, and those achievements contribute to the expectations placed on each new generation of footballers. Supporters naturally want to see their team compete for trophies and deliver convincing performances. However, the scrutiny surrounding individual mistakes has intensified with the growth of social media, instant replays and continuous football coverage. A single decision can become a major talking point long after the final whistle. The support structure around players, including coaches, teammates and family members, can help them manage these demands. item.title: Week 8 Fantasy Football Mailbag: Can Managers Comfortably Start Both Kyren Williams and Blake Corum?
item.description: Los Angeles Rams running back Kyren Williams (23) rushes the ball past Las Vegas Raiders cornerback Hezekiah Masses (35) at Allegiant Stadium. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The 2026 NFL season is moving quickly, and Week 8 kicks off Thursday with a matchup between the Carolina Panthers and Green Bay Packers. Ahead of Thursday's kickoff and this weekend's slate of games, fantasy football managers have endless decisions to make. In this week's installment of our fantasy football mailbag, which questions are eating away at managers? Note: Feel free to reach out to me on Twitter so I can answer your fantasy football questions in future articles. All stats used in this article are from PFF or Sumer Sports unless stated otherwise. Fantasy rankings and fantasy point totals are courtesy of FantasyPros . Can Fantasy Football Managers Feel Comfortable Starting Kyren Williams and Blake Corum? During the Los Angeles Rams' 35-21 win over the Las Vegas Raiders, Sean McVay deployed a heavy dose of both Kyren Williams and Blake Corum. Williams and Corum combined for 33 carries, 192 rushing yards, and 2 rushing TDs against the Raiders. In Week 7, Williams played a season-low 51.0% snap rate, but he still scored 18.1 fantasy points. Williams is tied with Jonathan Taylor as the RB6 in fantasy points per game (19.6) this season. Meanwhile, Corum logged his second-highest snap rate (44.0%) of the season in Week 7, earning a season-best 17.1 fantasy points. Corum has posted 14-plus fantasy points in three straight outings, and he's tied with Williams as the RB16 in fantasy points per game (15.8) since Week 5. With the Rams dealing with various injuries on offense, they could lean on their effective rushing attack to offset their absences. Between Williams and Corum, Williams should certainly be trusted more due to his usage in the passing game and in pass protection. While both Williams and Corum may not both be startable in games where Los Angeles isn't favored, they are both viable in Week 8 against the Los Angeles Chargers. Fantasy rankings and fantasy point totals are courtesy of FantasyPros . Can Fantasy Football Managers Feel Comfortable Starting Kyren Williams and Blake Corum? During the Los Angeles Rams' 35-21 win over the Las Vegas Raiders, Sean McVay deployed a heavy dose of both Kyren Williams and Blake Corum. Which Moves Should Managers Proactively Make Ahead of the Trade Deadline? The NFL trade deadline isn't until Tuesday, November 10, but fantasy football managers should be proactive about potential moves. Which moves should managers make before the trade deadline arrives? Buy Low on Josh Downs The Indianapolis Colts have already begun selling ahead of the trade deadline, and Josh Downs could use a change of scenery as the WR58 in fantasy points per game (8.2). Buy Low on Breece Hall The New York Jets are 2-5, and Braelon Allen has proven that he is capable of being a featured back in this offense amid Breece Hall's absence. Even if Hall isn't traded by the Jets, he's an ideal buy-low candidate as he'll either be a focal point of New York's offense or see a boost in another offense. Sign Seth McGowan Seth McGowan might be a rookie seventh-round pick who is 25 years old, but Jonathan Taylor could be on his way out of Indy. McGowan is a valuable handcuff right now, and he could become a featured back if Taylor is traded elsewhere soon. Buy Low on Brian Thomas Jr. Brian Thomas Jr. has fallen out of favor in the Jacksonville Jaguars' WR room, but he's still only 24 years old and had an extremely productive rookie season in 2024. The hope is that Thomas lands on a team that doesn't shoehorn him into a sacrificial X role where he's just running cardio. Is it Time to Panic About Derrick Henry? Father time tends to be unforgiving for aging RBs, but Derrick Henry has fended it off up to this point. However, Henry has scored fewer than six fantasy points in back-to-back games, and he's totaled 103 rushing yards on 34 carries during that span. While Henry's longest run is 17 yards over the last four weeks, the All-Pro back deserves some patience with Lamar Jackson nearing a return from a three-week absence. Additionally, the Baltimore Ravens have dealt with multiple injuries to the interior of their offensive line. Over the next four weeks, Henry faces the Buffalo Bills, Jacksonville Jaguars, Los Angeles Chargers, and Carolina Panthers. The Bills, Chargers, and Panthers are all allowing the 14th-most schedule-adjusted fantasy points per game or worse to RBs this season. If Henry struggles during that stretch, then it may be time to express concern. Hopefully everyone's fantasy football squads enjoy plenty of success in Week 8! item.title: Inaugural Major League Nations Cup Kicks Off The Big Professional Pickleball Association Worlds Week In Dallas
item.description: St. Louis Shock teammates Kate Fahey (L) and Anna Bright (R) team up again for Team USA in the 2026 MLP Nation's cup. MLP Now that the Professional Pickleball Association ’s top players have finished up their Australasian swing (with two Cup-level events in the last two weeks in the Australia Cup two weeks ago and the Hong Kong Slam last week ), it’s time for the biggest event on the PPA’s schedule; the 2026 World Championships . In each of the last two years, the tour has held a Major League Pickleball (MLP) event during the first weekend of the 10-day event; a round of playoffs in 2024 and the MLP Cup in 2025. This year, they’ve created a new MLP event that will serve to highlight the global growth of the pro game: the 2026 MLP Nation’s Cup . The league announced the event back in July , then started releasing the projected rosters for the 8-team competition in mid-September on their social media platforms. In this post, we’ll preview the rosters, talk about who may or may not have been a better pick for the teams, preview the group stages, and then offer some predictions. This event is of particular interest to this observer in part due to the previously announced PPA-World Cup partnership . This event seems like a dry run of future Olympic-style competitions, ones that could be a precursor to actual Olympic games involvement at some point in the future. We’re a ways from that point, organizationally and from a participation perspective, but having the world’s best players contractually enabled to compete in this style of competition is a great first step. There’s several Frenchmen who should be here (Khlif, Devilliers, Auvergne), plus Jaume Martinez Vich claims Spain as his homeland, plus there’s some solid Germans (Martin Emmrich, Pat Smith) and English players (Laville comes to mind) who probably would be better picks here. In this post, we’ll preview the rosters, talk about who may or may not have been a better pick for the teams, preview the group stages, and then offer some predictions. This event is of particular interest to this observer in part due to the previously announced PPA-World Cup partnership . We’re a ways from that point, organizationally and from a participation perspective, but having the world’s best players contractually enabled to compete in this style of competition is a great first step. Rosters for the Nations Cup Teams Chai-Yi "Zoey" Wang leads the way for team Asia Domestic. MLP Group A Asia Domestic : Augie Ge (China), Len Yang (China), Jonathan Truong (Vietnam) Milan Rane (India), Zoey Wang (Chinese Taipei), Jamie Wei (Chinese Taipei) Europe-West Will MacKinnon (Scotland), DJ Young (Spain), Theo Platel (France) Judit Castillo (Spain), Helena Jansen (Spain), Estee Widdershoven (Belgium) Canada Blaine Hovenier, Armaan Jiwa Mawji, Ryan Torresin Victoria DiMuzio, Layne Sleeth, Angie Walker USA Ben Johns, CJ Klinger, Will Howells Tyra Black, Anna Bright, Kate Fahey Thoughts on the Rosters: The Europe-West men seems like it could have been improved. There’s several Frenchmen who should be here (Khlif, Devilliers, Auvergne), plus Jaume Martinez Vich claims Spain as his homeland, plus there’s some solid Germans (Martin Emmrich, Pat Smith) and English players (Laville comes to mind) who probably would be better picks here. I think contract situations come into play for sure, but Europe West’s weaker men’s side may be their downfall. Canada’s rosters are missing their best female in Parenteau but otherwise the roster looks pretty solid. In the meantime, how does this event go on without Anna Leigh Waters representing USA? I’m frankly shocked that an “optional” MLP event has Johns but not Waters, given ALW’s devotion to the format. With all due respect to the USA rosters, a full strength men’s side includes both Patriquin and Tardio, with consideration to Alshon and JW Johnson. Honestly, they should have fielded two USA teams, perhaps one just from Boca Raton and its suburbs. Watch for a possible replacement for Black, who seems to have injured her hand in Asia. Group B Texas teammates Nico Acevedo (L) and Eric Oncins (center) will suit up for team Latin America this weekend. MLP` Asia International Hong kit “Jack: Wong (Hong Kong, China), Tama Shimabukuro (Hawaii), Jimmy Liong (Malaysia) Rika Fujiwara (Japan); Lingwei Kong (China), Macy Ybanez (Philippines) Australia Mitch Hargreaves, George Wall, Chris Crouch Sahra Dennehy, Danni-Elle Townsend, Sarah Burr Europe-East Andrei Daescu (Romania); Ivan Jakovlevic (Croatia), Arwid Dahlin (Sweden) Tina Pisnik (Slovenia); Daria Walczak (Poland), Lina Padegimaite (Lithuania); Latin America Nico Acevedo (Chile), Eric Oncins (Brazil), Rafa Lenhard (Brazil); Mari Humberg (Brazil), Alexa Schull (Puerto Rico), Carlota Trevino (Mexico) Thoughts on the Rosters: Team Asia could have picked from a slew of players and frankly could have fielded individual country teams from Vietnam, China, and Japan and have them be as good as some of these other countries. As they stand, They’ll certainly be a tough out. Some of Australia’s best players aren’t PPA signed, leaving them on the sidelines for this competition, not the least of which is Andie Dikosavljevic, who is probably a top-4 singles player right now in the world. The Eastern European team is going to be very tough, but the Latin America team could be the dark horse in this competition, with Acevedo teaming up with his Dallas Flash MLP teammate Oncins and a red-hot Humberg leading the line. Last minute replacements: Mikolaj Biedermann (Poland) was replaced on the Eastern European team by Jakovlevic. Shimabukuro replaced Hien Truong on the Asia Int’l team, for which he’s eligible by virtue of his parents. Group Stage and Overall Event Predictions Group play will feature two groups of four playing a round robin. Friday and Saturday will feature group stage, then Sunday a knockout between (presumably) the two top teams from each group. Group A: Asia Domestic, Europe-West, Canada, USA Group B: Asia International, Australia, Europe-East, Latin America Here’s how I think the groups play out. Group A will be a 3-0 win for Team USA of course, but who takes the second spot in the knockouts? I think Asia Domestic has the advantage here, with slightly stronger sides than Canada and Europe-West. Canada finishes 3rd, Europe West last. Group B is tough. I like all four teams. I can see a situation where we have three teams go 2-1 and tie for the top. The addition of Tama to the Asia team makes this a really difficult one to call. It is never wise to pick against Daescu or Pisnik, making the Eastern European team tough. But I think the PPA talent on Latin America will make the difference. I think the Asian team squeaks out 2nd place. Semis and Finals Prediction: Semis 1: USA over Asia International Semis 2: Latin America over Asia Domestic Final: Team USA wins MLP Nation’s Cup Group play begins Friday, October 30 at 11am EST/10 a.m. Central. Tune in to PickleballTv.com for coverage. This article was originally published on Forbes.com

item.title: Should Brewers Have Gone To Jacob Misiorowski With 12th Inning Lead?
item.description: Milwaukee Brewers pitcher Jacob Misiorowski In the 12th inning of Game 4 of the World Series, Milwaukee Brewers rookie Cooper Pratt delivered a home run that seemed destined to be played on replay for the rest of time in Milwaukee, but the Tampa Bay Rays scored two runs off Shane Drohan to walk it off in the bottom of the inning. Both teams taxed their bullpens in Game 4, and with a title on the line, the Brewers gave the ball to Drohan. To that point, in what was a bullpen game, the Brewers had used Dustin May, JoJo Romero, Abner Uribe, DL Hall, Trevor Megill, Aaron Ashby and Antonio Senzatela. The only pitchers available were Kyle Harrison, Brandon Woodruff, Jacob Misiorowski, Logan Henderson and Robert Gasser. Gasser started Game 3, Woodruff closed out Game 3 and Harrison has not pitched in October. None of them were real options, but with a title on the line, the Brewers did not go to their Cy Young Award frontrunner. Drohan had made one outing all postseason, as an opener against the Los Angeles Dodgers, and he was not great. To give him the ball in the 12th inning was certainly puzzling, especially when they could have given the ball to Misiorowski. Looking for the perfect gift for a baseball player in your life? Check out our brand new baseball lifestyle brand! To be fair, Drohan came in with a man on base after Joey Ortiz made an error that allowed Junior Caminero to reach base to start the inning. Drohan gave up some ground balls that found holes, and a high chopper over Jake Bauers with the bases loaded ended the game. While going to Misiorowski seems like the right move, the Brewers had one eye on the future in a close game that they used most of their arms in. If they went to Misiorowski and the Rays still won, he would have needed to start Game 5 on Wednesday after throwing in Game 4. However, it seems like Pat Murphy did not trust his ace's ability to get the job done in the 12th on three days of rest. If Misiorowski comes in and gets three outs, there is no Game 5 to plan for. It seems like Murphy was more concerned with making sure the team had a plan for Game 5 than winning Game 4. It's easy to criticize decisions after the fact, and Murphy is a two-time Manager of the Year Award winner. The reality is, the Brewers now have Misiorowski lined up in a closeout game while the Rays may have to resort to pitching madness. However, it seems like Pat Murphy did not trust his ace's ability to get the job done in the 12th on three days of rest. If Misiorowski comes in and gets three outs, there is no Game 5 to plan for. It seems like Murphy was more concerned with making sure the team had a plan for Game 5 than winning Game 4. It's easy to criticize decisions after the fact, and Murphy is a two-time Manager of the Year Award winner. The reality is, the Brewers now have Misiorowski lined up in a closeout game while the Rays may have to resort to pitching madness. More MLB: Brewers' Jackson Chourio Stands Alone As Only Player To Do This Twice In Postseason

item.title: Fernandes tells Carrick he is committed to turning season around in clear-the-air talks
item.description: Manchester United captain expected to return to line-up Squad have positive meeting with under-pressure coach Michael Carrick and Bruno Fernandes held clear-the-air talks on Tuesday after the Manchester United’s captain criticised the manager’s tactics last week, with him now expected to start at Chelsea on Saturday. Carrick and Fernandes met before training on Tuesday morning at United’s Carrington training base. The 32-year-old, it is understood, offered the manager assurances that he is fully committed and intent on trying to turn the team’s season around. There was also a squad meeting with Carrick at which the rest of the players made the same vow. Continue reading...

item.title: Stephan gives updates on four QPR stars ahead of Southampton clash
item.description: Stephan gives updates on four QPR stars ahead of Southampton clash QPR boss Julien Stephan is hopeful Ilias Chair, Boy Kemper and Alfie Lloyd will all be available for Saturday’s trip to Southampton. Jake Clarke-Salter remains a doubt, but Stephan offered a positive update on the other three players as the R’s prepare for their visit to the south coast. “Boy didn’t train but, and I’m not a doctor, I think it will be okay for the end of the week,” Stephan told West London Sport . “There is more of a question mark around Jake Clarke-Salter. I don’t know if he will be available by the end of the week.” Chair, meanwhile, has not featured since last month , while Lloyd has missed QPR’s last two matches. “Alfie has trained in part of the session and now hopefully he will be completely involved, and the same for Illy,” he said. “I want to say it’s quite positive, but I have to wait until the big training session on Wednesday to be sure that they are available for the next game. It’s a little bit early in the week. “But it’s quite positive that for both it will be okay.”

item.title: Erik Spoelstra diagnoses Giannis Antetokounmpo-led Heat's biggest weakness
item.description: Erik Spoelstra diagnoses Giannis Antetokounmpo-led Heat's biggest weakness originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Many factors can explain why an NBA team starts its campaign winless. The Miami Heat have many factors to consider after losing four straight games to the Minnesota Timberwolves , Detroit Pistons , Charlotte Hornets , and Dallas Mavericks . Some blamed Giannis Antetokounmpo while others pointed fingers at Bam Adebayo. Coach Erik Spoelstra says the change shouldn't come from a player; it's in their schematic system. The Heat head coach said they have a glaring weakness to fix and laid out plans to do it. Spoelstra reveals Antetokounmpo-led Heat's biggest weakness Four losses don't come out of nowhere or from bad nights. Either the squad's schematics or rotations have problems. This is exactly how Coach Erik Spoelstra feels about the Heat's losing streak. Spoelstra wasn't blaming Giannis Antetokounmpo or Bam Adebayo. Instead, the head coach identified a major problem the Heat had to fix to get out of this four-game rut, via Eric Nehm of The Athletic. "We are going to have to execute in the halfcourt. There’s no way around that. You can’t play a pace game for a full 48 minutes. You also do need to be able to execute in the half court, and that’s where our spacing and our principles become so vital to open up driving lanes and open up opportunities for our guys to make plays," the Heat head coach declared. True enough, Coach Spoelstra does make a great point about the Heat. The only major statistical category where they rank within the top 10 in the NBA is pace. Antetokounmpo and Adebayo run an offense that has a 103.2 pace; that's good for eighth in the NBA. In every other category, the Heat falter. For starters, they have a -12.4 net rating that's 27th in the NBA. This is due to their 105.7 offensive rating, 27th in the league, and 118.0 defensive rating, 22nd in the league. They have a .500 eFG% that ranks 24th in the league, while their ORB% of .211 ranks 28th in the NBA. This suggests they can't get shots off efficiently and struggle to clean the offensive glass for second-chance opportunities. Defensively, the same woes show up. The Heat allow a .565 eFG%, the fifth-worst in the NBA. This suggests problems in point-of-attack defense and overall shot contests. Their DRB% of 70.1% is also just 19th in the league. item.title: Sandpaper haunts Australia in Cape Town: South Africa fans wave sandpaper to mock Nathan Lyon on Day 2 of 3rd Test
item.description: Sandpaper haunts Australia in Cape Town: South Africa fans wave sandpaper to mock Nathan Lyon on Day 2 of 3rd Test originally appeared on Cricket News . Add Cricket News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . KEY TAKEAWAYS: A South Africa fan waved sandpaper at Australia 's Nathan Lyon on the Newlands boundary on Day 2. Newlands is the ground where the 2018 ball-tampering scandal took place. Lyon ignored the taunt and carried on fielding. MORE: SA vs AUS 3rd Test Day 2 2026 live scorecard, toss winner, winning probability, result and highlights from Cape Town South Africa fans wave sandpaper at Nathan Lyon in Cape Town Nathan Lyon spent part of Day 2 fielding on the boundary at Newlands, in front of a crowd that had worked out exactly which prop to bring. A fan held up a sheet of sandpaper and offered it to him, suggesting Australia might find it useful given how little the pitch had done for their bowlers. Lyon did not take the bait, acknowledging the crowd and getting on with the over. The exchange was filmed from the stands and has been circulating since. "SOUTH AFRICAN FABS ARE WILD IN TERMS OF TROLLING. A fan was showing a sandpaper to Nathan Lyon and telling him that I would help them as wickets were not falling," one fan account wrote . "Lyon handled the situation perfectly like a professional. These banters are so funny to watch." SOUTH AFRICAN FABS ARE WILD IN TERMS OF TROLLING A fan was showing a sandpaper to Nathan Lyon and telling him that I would help them as wickets were not falling Lyon handled the situation perfectly like a professional These banters are so funny to watch — (@CRICBALLY) October 28, 2026 Every Aussie knows the reason for the sandpaper, and the Proteas were not ready for their opponents to forget it throughout the game. MORE: Starc eclipses Warne's Newlands figures with 6-fer as SA collapse History of Sandpaper at Newlands, Cape Town Newlands is where it happened. Cameron Bancroft was filmed using sandpaper on the ball during the third Test of the 2018 series at this ground, a scandal that cost Steve Smith and David Warner 12-month bans, Bancroft nine months, and Darren Lehmann his job as coach. This series is the first time Australia have played a Test in South Africa since that tour, making the subject unavoidable from the moment the schedule came out. Justin Langer revisited it last week, arguing that Smith, Warner and Bancroft took the fall for cricketers everywhere and that the ball has barely reverse swung since. Lyon is one of four Australians in this side who played in the Cape Town Test eight years ago, alongside Mitchell Starc, Josh Hazlewood and Pat Cummins. None of the four was implicated, which is part of what makes him an odd target beyond simply being the man nearest the fence. item.title: Green Bay Packers’ Matt LaFleur calls for consistency after controversial Lions game
item.description: The Green Bay Packers dropped to 4-3 following a narrow 20-17 defeat against the Detroit Lions in Week 7. While controversial officiating decisions left many feeling that Green Bay had been on the wrong end of several calls, head coach Matt LaFleur chose a measured approach when addressing the referees on Tuesday. LaFleur avoided escalating the debate over the disputed calls when reporters raised the issue once more. As Ryan Wood of USA Today Sports reported, the 46-year-old coach recognized the difficulty officials face when they must judge fast moving plays in real time. Rather than dwell on specific decisions, LaFleur stressed that he simply wants the officiating to remain consistent from game to game. “I don’t think officiating in this league is very easy. I really don’t. I think things happen quickly, and there’s some bang-bang decisions they have to make. So I don’t think they have an easy job. All you want as a coach is consistency,” commented the Packers head coach. Matt LaFleur and the Packers against the Lions Oct 25, 2026; Detroit, Michigan, USA; Packers head coach Matt LaFleur reacts after a call during the third quarter against the Detroit Lions at Ford Field. Mandatory Credit: Lon Horwedel-Imagn Images Several disputed calls against the Packers late in the second half helped Detroit close out its victory. One of the most debated decisions came in the third quarter, when officials flagged defensive end Brenton Cox for roughing the passer, drawing an angry reaction from future Hall of Fame quarterback and broadcaster Tom Brady . Additional penalties against defensive tackle Devonte Wyatt, defensive tackle Karl Brooks, and quarterback Jordan Love also sparked confusion among viewers. NFL coaches and players risk hefty fines or suspensions if they publicly criticize game officials. That restriction could explain Matt LaFleur’s comments on Tuesday. Regardless, the Packers will turn their attention to Week 8, when they host the Carolina Panthers on “Thursday Night Football.” More Packers news from Wisconsin Sports Heroics Packers running back Josh Jacobs (8) runs against Detroit Lions during the first half at Ford Field in Detroit on Sunday, Oct. 25, 2026. item.title: Opponent Breakdown: Stanford Cardinal Offense
item.description: PALO ALTO, CA - OCTOBER 23: Running back Micah Ford carries the ball during an ACC college football game against the NC State Wolfpack played on October 23, 2026 at Stanford Stadium in Palo Alto, California. (Photo by David Madison/Getty Images) | Getty Images Jeff Brohm has a handful of losses during his time at Louisville that could be deemed “bad”. His loss to Stanford in 2024 would qualify for that classification. Stanford came into that game with a 2-7 record, with one of those wins being against an FCS school. They were more prepared than the Cards, and they played as if their season was on the line. The Cardinal will come to Louisville this time around with an improved program and two upset victories in the ACC to their name. Stanford hit the portal this offseason to shore up a quarterback position that has struggled for the last few years. Davis Warren landed back in his home state after spending some time as a starter at Michigan. Warren has shown that he has the talent to make plays in this offense, but he has been extremely inconsistent and has not shown the ability to play at a truly high level. Against Georgia Tech and NC State, Warren threw for over 300 yards and a combined 7 touchdowns. Outside of those games, he has been below average at best. Louisville has to find a way to pressure Warren, as that is when he has struggled this season. The key to the Stanford two-game winning streak has been Micah Ford at running back. The 6/225 junior has put up over 300 yards rushing over the last two weeks, while also being a threat in the passing game with over 100 yards receiving. His 9 yards per play over the last two games is comparable to Keyjuan Brown’s output for the season. The trend towards being an explosive player for this offense will need to end this week, as this offense goes as Ford goes. He has nearly twice as much all-purpose yardage as any other player on Stanford’s offense. Receiver is an interesting position for the Cardinal as they have one player who has shown the ability to break out in a game, but they have a few reliable guys overall. Caden High has two 100-yard games this year, and those games came against Georgia Tech and NC State. High showed up in the big games this year as a dynamic talent who can make plays at all three levels of the defense. He is the receiver they have to make a plan for this weekend. That has not been something this defense has been able to do a single time this season. JonAnthony Hall and Nico Brown are the other top receivers on the outside in this offense. Hall has been able to make a couple of big plays this year, while Brown has been an option in the red zone. Neither player has been a truly consistent threat this year, but they are plenty capable of stepping up to have a big game. This entire receiver group has feasted on zone coverage, so it would be nice to see the UofL secondary get a chance to challenge these guys in man coverage. The Cards also need to be aware of Benji Blackburn at tight end. He has been very good with 24 catches this year. The Stanford offensive line profiles as a solid group. They don’t give up a lot of negative plays, though they could be better at preventing sacks. Watching their games, I think some of the sacks are coverage sacks due to their receivers struggling to get open and Warren holding onto the ball. Warren is athletic enough to extend plays, but he doesn’t look to run when he doesn’t have an open option. The Cards have been very good at getting pressure and sacks in three of the last four halves of play. They will need to utilize the aggressive scheme they rolled out against FSU to force this line to show that they can protect the quarterback as well as open holes for Micah Ford.

item.title: National rumors persist about Rickard Rakell
item.description: It’s nothing new for veteran Penguins players to find their names being brought up on national panels and media outlets when it comes to potential trades. Lately, Rickard Rakell has been a popular name to share among the likes of Frank Seravalli, Nick Kypreos and Chris Johnston for early season chatter about potential names to keep an eye on for a possible trade. The trade talk is starting to pick up as the NHL regular season rolls into its fifth week. We’ve expanded our early Big Board to 20 names, starting with Dylan Larkin. Read more, from @reporterchris (unlocked 🔓) https://t.co/wnuhva47w2 — The Athletic (@TheAthletic) October 27, 2026 7. Rickard Rakell, Pittsburgh Penguins Age: 33 Position: RW Contract term: 2028 UFA Cap hit : $5 million No stranger to the Big Board in the past few years, Rakell may finally be in his final months with a Penguins team slowly transitioning to a younger group. He’s delivered an outsized amount of production on a reasonable contract, but it’s been a slow start for both player and team. Still, Rakell is an above-average finisher who has a history of holding his own when playing alongside highly skilled linemates. He’s scored at a 29-goal-per-82-game pace across the last four seasons. Frank Seravalli – Oilers NOW – Penguins | Rakell up for grabs. Bryan Rust will be up for grabs. That whole core outside of the big guns are all going to be in play and in talks and look for the Penguins to take Flyers on younger players around the league that have fallen out of… pic.twitter.com/GZfZ0h0AyV — R i N K Y (@RinkyReport) October 27, 2026 The last one from over the weekend might be the spiciest since it contains some specific information. Nick Kypreos: The Penguins have been ready to move on from Rickard Rakell since the summer, but couldn’t close a deal – Sportsnet (10/22) — NHL Rumour Report (@NHLRumourReport) October 27, 2026 That nugget makes the mind wander back to the behind the scenes video that the Ottawa Senators shared over the summer , where they were considering moving the 25th overall pick on draft night in June in exchange for an unnamed ‘roster player’ from the Penguins. Nothing further came to light regarding who was involved, but it’s not a huge stretch to imagine that could have been an effort to move Rakell in the summer as Kypreos mentioned. It also was unclear from the video if there were more parts involved than just one roster player and Ottawa’s 25th overall pick, which they ultimately elected to hang onto and use themselves, so it’s impossible to judge from the outside just what that exact proposal might have been – if it involved Rakell at all. As perhaps usual when it comes to Rakell, the value that the team views him considering his on ice contributions still outweigh the amount other NHL clubs are willing to offer. So then, as it is now, comes the lasting period of rumors and whispers with little other tangible information out there. Rakell’s name isn’t the only one being spoken about. There are

Rickard Rakell, Pittsburgh Penguins Age: 33 Position: RW Contract term: 2028 UFA Cap hit : $5 million No stranger to the Big Board in the past few years, Rakell may finally be in his final months with a Penguins team slowly transitioning to a younger group. He’s delivered an outsized amount of production on a reasonable contract, but it’s been a slow start for both player and team. Still, Rakell is an above-average finisher who has a history of holding his own when playing alongside highly skilled linemates. He’s scored at a 29-goal-per-82-game pace across the last four seasons. Frank Seravalli – Oilers NOW – Penguins | Rakell up for grabs. Bryan Rust will be up for grabs. That whole core outside of the big guns are all going to be in play and in talks and look for the Penguins to take Flyers on younger players around the league that have fallen out of… pic.twitter.com/GZfZ0h0AyV — R i N K Y (@RinkyReport) October 27, 2026 The last one from over the weekend might be the spiciest since it contains some specific information. Nick Kypreos: The Penguins have been ready to move on from Rickard Rakell since the summer, but couldn’t close a deal – Sportsnet (10/22) — NHL Rumour Report (@NHLRumourReport) October 27, 2026 That nugget makes the mind wander back to the behind the scenes video that the Ottawa Senators shared over the summer , where they were considering moving the 25th overall pick on draft night in June in exchange for an unnamed ‘roster player’ from the Penguins. Nothing further came to light regarding who was involved, but it’s not a huge stretch to imagine that could have been an effort to move Rakell in the summer as Kypreos mentioned. It also was unclear from the video if there were more parts involved than just one roster player and Ottawa’s 25th overall pick, which they ultimately elected to hang onto and use themselves, so it’s impossible to judge from the outside just what that exact proposal might have been – if it involved Rakell at all. As perhaps usual when it comes to Rakell, the value that the team views him considering his on ice contributions still outweigh the amount other NHL clubs are willing to offer. So then, as it is now, comes the lasting period of rumors and whispers with little other tangible information out there. Rakell’s name isn’t the only one being spoken about. There are various reports about the availability and potential likelihood of Bryan Rust and Erik Karlsson also making the rounds. Say enough names for long enough and it’s bound to come true eventually, though it’s very clear that many eyes outside of Pittsburgh are keeping a close eye on how the Penguins do in the standings in the immediate future and what pivots that Kyle Dubas and company might choose to make as they build their team for this season and potentially beyond.

item.title: 2026 PGA Tour fall: What players are on the bubble with 4 events left?
item.description: Where a player finishes in the FedExCup Fall standings after the RSM Classic decides his 2027 status. Here are the lines that matter: Final fall rank What it means for 2027 1 to 50 Already set. Spots in every '27 signature event. These players earn 0 fall points. 51 to 60 The Aon Next 10. Full status plus spots in the AT&T Pebble Beach Pro-Am and Genesis Invitational. 61 to 100 Full status. Entry to every full-field event and The Players Championship. 101 to 125 Conditional Tour status, with starts set by priority ranking and reshuffles; fully exempt on Korn Ferry Tour. 126 to 150 No PGA Tour card. Fully exempt on Korn Ferry Tour. 151 to 200 Conditional status on Korn Ferry Tour. The top 70 from the regular season locked up their 2027 cards by reaching the playoffs. Anyone outside the top 100 can try to win back a card at Q-School. Past winners and other exempt players keep their cards no matter where they rank. That is why Brooks Koepka and Tony Finau can sit at Nos. 106 and 107 without much worry. This is the second fall under the Tour's policy of awarding only 100 cards. For about four decades the cutoff sat at 125. The VidantaWorld Mexico Open this week is the fifth of eight fall events. The World Wide Technology Championship in Los Cabos follows next week, then the Austin Championship, concluding with the RSM Classic at Sea Island on Nov. 22, after which the standing will be final. Here are some notable players on the various bubbles halfway through the fall: Billy Horschel, No. 94 Horschel opened the fall exactly on the bubble, sitting at No. 100 when the Tour arrived in Asheville. A T-13 in Utah and a T-21 in Japan lifted him to 90th. He didn't play in Bermuda and dropped four spots, but is in this week's field. Horschel is an eight-time Tour winner and the 2014 FedExCup champion, but the exemption from those wins runs out with this season. He started 2026 at No. 53 in the world and had fallen more than a hundred places by September. His only top-10 of the year came at the Zurich Classic team event. VidantaWorld Mexico Open - Rd 1 The opening round of the VidantaWorld Mexico Open is underway at Vidanta Vallarta Golf Course in Vallarta, Mexico. Lucas Glover, No. 110 Glover began the fall one spot behind Horschel, the first man out. Six weeks later he is 110th on the list. Three years ago, Glover won the Wyndham and then the FedEx St. Jude at TPC Southwind in back-to-back weeks. The exemptions from those wins expired this year. This season he started at No. 64 in the world and earned his way into all eight signature events, then finished inside the top 20 in only one of them. A pair of top-5s in July kept him close, but he has not built on that success. Glover, chairman of the PGA Tour’s Player Advisory Council , turns 47 next month and is in his 23rd season on the PGA Tour. He is not competing this week. He's not in Mexico this week, and has the event in Austin that makes sense for him to be part of next month at Omni Barton Creek Resort & Spa. (Photo by Minas Panagiotakis/Getty Images) Getty Images Ben James, No. 63 James finished No. 1 in the 2026 PGA Tour University ranking after a Virginia career with seven wins and 35 top-10s in 46 starts. He turned pro in June and already holds a card through 2027. He is now playing for a place in those first two signature events. He has four top-5s in his first 10 pro starts and is looking for a breakthrough win this week in Mexico.

item.title: Alexis Mac Allister set for Liverpool exit
item.description: Alexis Mac Allister set for Liverpool exit Alexis Mac Allister (27) looks set to leave Liverpool at the end of the season, as per a report from Franco-Belgian journalist Sacha Tavolieri. The Argentine recently said that he was upset at not having been offered a contract extension by the Merseyside, whilst other teammates in midfield were seeing there deals renewed. And it would seem that a new contract is not forthcoming for the Argentina international. Liverpool are looking to rebuild their midfield in the summer of 2027 and Tavolieri understands that Mac Allister does not feature in their plans. With his deal at Anfield running until the summer of 2028, a departure at the end of the season is envisaged. Informed of this, the player’s entourage have already begun sounding out potential destinations. Clubs in La Liga, Serie A, and the Saudi Pro League have all been contacted and alerted to his availability. So far this season, Mac Allister has played 12 times and netted four goals. GFFN | Luke Entwistle

item.title: Pistons Reportedly Have Interest in Pairing Future Hall of Famer With Cade Cunningham
item.description: The Detroit Pistons may not be finished searching for another star to play alongside Cade Cunningham , and one of the NBA’s most accomplished guards remains an intriguing possibility. According to ESPN’s Vincent Goodwill, multiple members of the Pistons organization are interested in what Dallas Mavericks star Kyrie Irving could bring to Detroit. The nine-time All-Star has demonstrated an ability to thrive alongside ball-dominant superstars, something that could make him an excellent fit next to Cunningham. The interest is not entirely new, either. Detroit reportedly explored acquiring Irving earlier this year, suggesting the possibility deserves more attention than a random trade proposal. Oct 26, 2026; Miami, Florida, USA; Dallas Mavericks guard Kyrie Irving (11) looks on against the Miami Heat during the third quarter at Kaseya Center. Mandatory Credit: Sam Navarro-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Pistons Staff Reportedly Like Kyrie Irving In an October 9 report examining Detroit’s championship aspirations, Goodwill revealed that members of the organization are intrigued by Irving’s offensive abilities. “And if Detroit has the stomach to go after it this year, they could go after someone like Kyrie Irving in Dallas — several staffers are fond of Irving’s game, shot creation and malleability next to ball-dominant stars like James and Luka Doncic,” Goodwill wrote . That is an interesting development for a Pistons team still searching for a dependable secondary offensive creator. Cunningham has established himself as one of the NBA’s premier young players, but Detroit’s postseason shortcomings exposed the difficulty of relying too heavily on one player to generate offense. Irving could change that equation. The 34-year-old guard has already won an NBA championship alongside LeBron James and reached another NBA Finals while playing alongside Luka Doncic in Dallas. His ball-handling, perimeter shooting, and ability to create difficult shots make him a potentially valuable addition to Detroit’s offense. item.content:encoded: The Detroit Pistons may not be finished searching for another star to play alongside Cade Cunningham , and one of the NBA’s most accomplished guards remains an intriguing possibility. According to ESPN’s Vincent Goodwill, multiple members of the Pistons organization are interested in what Dallas Mavericks star Kyrie Irving could bring to Detroit. The nine-time All-Star has demonstrated an ability to thrive alongside ball-dominant superstars, something that could make him an excellent fit next to Cunningham. The interest is not entirely new, either. Detroit reportedly explored acquiring Irving earlier this year, suggesting the possibility deserves more attention than a random trade proposal. Oct 26, 2026; Miami, Florida, USA; Dallas Mavericks guard Kyrie Irving (11) looks on against the Miami Heat during the third quarter at Kaseya Center. Mandatory Credit: Sam Navarro-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Pistons Staff Reportedly Like Kyrie Irving In an October 9 report examining Detroit’s championship aspirations, Goodwill revealed that members of the organization are intrigued by Irving’s offensive abilities. “And if Detroit has the stomach to go after it this year, they could go after someone like Kyrie Irving in Dallas — several staffers are fond of Irving’s game, shot creation and malleability next to ball-dominant stars like James and Luka Doncic,” Goodwill wrote . That is an interesting development for a Pistons team still searching for a dependable secondary offensive creator. Cunningham has established himself as one of the NBA’s premier young players, but Detroit’s postseason shortcomings exposed the difficulty of relying too heavily on one player to generate offense. Irving could change that equation. The 34-year-old guard has already won an NBA championship alongside LeBron James and reached another NBA Finals while playing alongside Luka Doncic in Dallas. His ball-handling, perimeter shooting, and ability to create difficult shots make him a potentially valuable addition to Detroit’s offense. Detroit Previously Explored an Irving Trade The Pistons’ connection to Irving dates back several months. In June, NBA insider Marc Stein reported that Detroit had contacted Dallas about a potential Irving trade . Minnesota was also among the teams that had reportedly inquired about the veteran guard. However, Dallas president of basketball operations Masai Ujiri reportedly informed interested teams that Irving was not available. That is an important distinction. Although Detroit has demonstrated interest in Irving, there is no confirmed indication that the Mavericks have changed their position or that the two franchises are currently negotiating a trade. As we previously reported when examining Detroit’s aggressive offseason approach , president of basketball operations Trajan Langdon explored several major acquisitions, including Irving, Kevin Durant, and Kawhi Leonard. Detroit ultimately decided against sacrificing significant assets for a blockbuster acquisition. Would Irving Be Worth the Risk? There is little doubt that a healthy Irving would give Detroit another legitimate offensive weapon. However, there are several reasons Langdon would need to approach a potential deal carefully. Irving missed the entire 2025-26 season while recovering from a torn ACL, creating uncertainty about how quickly he can return to his previous level of production. His contract also presents a challenge. Irving is earning approximately $39.5 million this season and holds a player option for 2027-28. Acquiring him would require Detroit to construct a financially workable trade while considering how much of its young core and future draft capital it would be willing to surrender. That becomes especially important after the Pistons made substantial financial commitments to Cunningham, Jalen Duren, and Ausar Thompson. Detroit has already explored other potential backcourt upgrades , including the possibility of acquiring Austin Reaves. The continued discussion surrounding Irving highlights the same underlying question: Does Cunningham need another elite shot creator for the Pistons to reach the NBA Finals? If Irving returns healthy, the answer could be worth exploring. Pistons Have a Difficult Decision Ahead The Pistons are no longer a rebuilding team simply hoping to reach the playoffs. After winning 60 games last season, expectations have changed considerably in Detroit. Langdon must now determine whether continuing to develop the current roster is the best path forward or whether adding an established superstar could accelerate the team’s championship pursuit. Irving would undoubtedly be an aggressive gamble. He is 34, coming off a significant injury, and carries a substantial salary. Dallas has also shown no confirmed willingness to trade him. But the possibility of pairing his offensive creativity with Cunningham’s all-around brilliance is understandably appealing. Detroit has already asked about Irving once. If the Mavericks eventually become willing to listen, Langdon may have another difficult decision to make.

item.title: Where to watch Rays vs. Brewers today: Channel, time, TV schedule, live stream for World Series Game 5
item.description: Where to watch Rays vs. Brewers today: Channel, time, TV schedule, live stream for World Series Game 5 originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . We'll have at least one more day of baseball in 2026. The Tampa Bay Rays finally picked up their first win of the World Series, rallying in the 12th inning for a 4-3 victory over the Milwaukee Brewers in Game 4 Tuesday night. It was only Milwaukee's second defeat this postseason and extended the series to a fifth game, which is set for Wednesday. At the very least, the Rays prevented the Brewers from becoming the first team to sweep in a Fall Classic since the Giants blanked the Tigers in 2012, but the odds remain heavily in Milwaukee's favor. Of the 44 times MLB teams have gone up 3-0 in a best-of-seven series, 39 have clinched by the fifth game. The 2004 Red Sox remain the only team to win a series after dropping the first three games with their legendary ALCS comeback that year against the Yankees. Aside from the raw probabilities involved, the Rays also face the unpleasant task of facing Jacob Misiorowski again Wednesday. The likely NL Cy Young winner beat them in the series opener and will undoubtedly be gassed up to clinch the title. On the other side, it'll be all hands on deck for Kevin Cash. His Game 1 starter, Nick Martinez, pitched two innings in relief Tuesday and likely won't be available, so Tampa Bay will have to get creative. Can the Rays send the series back to Milwaukee, or will the Brewers return home with a trophy? Here's everything you need to know about watching Game 5 of the World Series. Where to watch Rays vs. Brewers today TV channels: Fox Live streams: Fubo , DIRECTV Fox will have coverage of Game 5 of the World Series between the Brewers and Rays, with Joe Davis and John Smoltz set to call the game. Fans looking for a streaming option can use DIRECTV or Fubo . Fubo offers a free trial for new subscribers, so you can try the service before you buy. Stream ESPN, ABC, CBS, Fox, NBC and 100+ top channels of live TV and sports without cable. (Participating plans only. Taxes and fees may apply.) World Series Game 5 start time Date : Wednesday, Oct. 28 Time : 8 p.m. ET | 7 p.m. CT Game 5 of the World Series between the Rays and Brewers is scheduled to begin Wednesday at 8 p.m. from Tropicana Field in St. Petersburg, Florida. World Series radio station Radio station: SiriusXM Channels 202 (Rays), 203 (Brewers) SiriusXM will have all radio broadcasts of the 2026 World Series games between the Brewers and Rays. The Rays broadcast will be on channel 202, and the Brewers broadcast will be on channel 203. item.title: 700 Yards? Washington High School QB Breaks Single-Game High School Record
item.description: Courtesy of Ryan Harrington Washington State quarterback commit Ryan Harrington put together one of the most remarkable performances in high school football history Friday night. The Anacortes High School senior threw for 704 yards and 10 touchdowns in a 68-20 victory over Sehome, breaking Washington’s single-game passing record and tying the state record for touchdown passes in a game. Harrington completed 26 of 38 passes in the victory, surpassing the previous state record of 613 passing yards set by Brett Rypien of Shadle Park in 2013. Rypien went on to play at Boise State before reaching the NFL , where he currently plays for the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. Harrington’s performance puts him among a small group of high school quarterbacks nationally to surpass 700 passing yards in a single game. According to reports, the last quarterback to throw for more than 700 yards in a high school game was Peyton Houston, who passed for 817 yards for Evangel Christian Academy in Louisiana in 2024. Ryan Harrington Ties Washington Touchdown Record Harrington’s 10 touchdown passes tied the Washington Interscholastic Activities Association’s single-game record. Nathaniel Holcomb of Puyallup set the mark in 2016, while Sam Huard of Kennedy Catholic matched it in 2018. Huard is the son of former NFL quarterback Damon Huard. Harrington reached the milestone in dramatic fashion. With 20 seconds remaining in Friday’s game, he connected with fellow senior Dre Quintino on a 49-yard touchdown pass, giving him his 10th scoring pass of the night. Harrington said he had been informed of the touchdown record during the game and wanted the opportunity to reach it. “I don’t like to play selfish,” Harrington told SI.com. “But this is the one time I wanted to be selfish.” The passing-yardage record came as a surprise. Harrington learned just how much he had accomplished later that night after receiving a text message from Anacortes coach Justin Portz, according to SI.com’s report. “It didn’t feel real,” Harrington said. Portz said the opportunity to make history became clear as the game progressed and Sehome continued to blitz defensively. “I was thinking last night, in the moment, that maybe there was a coach out there who really feels the right thing to do is take a knee,” Portz said. “I was thinking, ‘You do not get this opportunity very often to let one of your kids break a record, so let’s go for it!’” “We didn’t go into the game thinking it, but it was presented to us (by how Sehome was blitzing so often on defense) – so why not put this exclamation point on his career at Anacortes.” Washington State Commit Continues Historic Season Harrington’s record-setting night continued what has been a dominant stretch for the senior quarterback. In his previous game, a 49-13 victory over Bellingham, Harrington threw for 413 yards and six touchdowns. Over the past two games, he has combined for 1,117 passing yards and 16 touchdowns, putting him among the most productive quarterbacks i

Harrington said he had been informed of the touchdown record during the game and wanted the opportunity to reach it. “I don’t like to play selfish,” Harrington told SI.com. “But this is the one time I wanted to be selfish.” The passing-yardage record came as a surprise. Harrington learned just how much he had accomplished later that night after receiving a text message from Anacortes coach Justin Portz, according to SI.com’s report. “It didn’t feel real,” Harrington said. Portz said the opportunity to make history became clear as the game progressed and Sehome continued to blitz defensively. “I was thinking last night, in the moment, that maybe there was a coach out there who really feels the right thing to do is take a knee,” Portz said. “I was thinking, ‘You do not get this opportunity very often to let one of your kids break a record, so let’s go for it!’” “We didn’t go into the game thinking it, but it was presented to us (by how Sehome was blitzing so often on defense) – so why not put this exclamation point on his career at Anacortes.” Washington State Commit Continues Historic Season Harrington’s record-setting night continued what has been a dominant stretch for the senior quarterback. In his previous game, a 49-13 victory over Bellingham, Harrington threw for 413 yards and six touchdowns. Over the past two games, he has combined for 1,117 passing yards and 16 touchdowns, putting him among the most productive quarterbacks in the country. Harrington has thrown for 2,424 yards and 32 touchdowns this season, helping Anacortes build a 7-1 record. The 6-foot-1 quarterback also has an impressive postseason history. He has helped Anacortes win two Class 2A state championships, including during his sophomore season, when he threw for more than 1,700 yards while sharing quarterback duties. Harrington passed for 3,372 yards as a junior as Anacortes finished 7-3. Now committed to Washington State, Harrington has added a historic individual achievement to his high school résumé. His 704-yard performance broke a state record that had stood for 13 years and placed him among a select group of quarterbacks to reach that milestone nationally. item.title: Soccer fans call out Dave Portnoy for his video mocking Arsenal in a Tottenham jersey
item.description: Photo by Gary Gershoff/Getty Images Dave Portnoy went viral after mocking English soccer champions Arsenal for their loss against Fleetwood Town. Unfortunately, a lot of the replies were making fun of him. The world of soccer saw a monumental upset in the Carabao Cup on Tuesday night. Reigning Premier League champions Arsenal lost on penalties against Fleetwood Town, a club which is struggling in the fourth division of the professional soccer pyramid. Naturally, this was big news, and fans of rival clubs were out in force to make fun of Arsenal following their loss. Surprisingly enough, Barstool Sports CEO Dave Portnoy was among their numbers. However, it was the jersey he was sporting which led to his ridicule backfiring on him. Dave Portnoy got trolled for his Tottenham Hotspur fandom while trying to mock their rivals Arsenal are a club based in North London. Their biggest rivals are another local North London club, Tottenham Hotspur. Portnoy is a self-confessed Tottenham fan, so it makes sense that he would try to gloat after this poor display by the Gunners. However, Spurs themselves are in shambles as a club. Having faced a relegation battle last season, they are currently in 14th place and are out of the Carabao Cup as well. All these points came up as fans made fun of Portnoy for trying to talk trash when he supports Tottenham. “True Spurs supporter, your only thing to get excited over is Arsenal losing,” one fan commented. “Your team is 14th in the Premier league by the way and are already out of the Carabao Cup,” another fan said. “Fleetwood did something the Spurs haven’t done in 1,624 days,” a third fan explained. “Dude your team might be facing relegation,” one comment pointed out. “Putting the kit on was brave. The kit immediately betraying you was inevitable,” claimed a fifth fan. “Coming from a guy in a Tottenham shirt I’d be very quiet,” a sixth fan observed. There is no doubting that this was an extremely embarrassing loss for Arsenal. However, being a Spurs fan is likely to mean there isn’t much high ground for someone like Portnoy to be ridiculing his rivals from. Overall, it seems everyone involved in the story got their fair share of mockery. item.title: Here's The Clever Way Jayson Tatum Got So Open For His Game-Winner
item.description: Here's The Clever Way Jayson Tatum Got So Open For His Game-Winner originally appeared on NESN . Add NESN as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Jayson Tatum was going to get the final shot. Joe Mazzulla just had to figure out how to get him open. On the second night of a back-to-back, Tatum led the Boston Celtics to victory over the Brooklyn Nets with 40 points, eight assists and five rebounds. He shot 10-for-20 from the field and made a career-high 18 free throws on 22 attempts. If that wasn't enough, Tatum also hit the game-winning jump shot in overtime. It was a big-time shot from Tatum, but Mazzulla's fingerprints were all over the play. MORE: Jayson Tatum Is Already On One of the Best Stretches of His NBA Career How Jayson Tatum Got So Open vs. Nets Down by one point with 2.3 seconds left, Mazzulla closed the game with Tatum, Payton Pritchard, Derrick White, Sam Hauser and Paul George. White was in charge of inbounding the ball. Tatum parked himself on the right block, Hauser and George stood close to each other on the opposite side of the court and Pritchard started in the backcourt. As soon as the referee handed the ball to White, Tatum sprinted toward Pritchard to set a screen. NBA That put the Nets in a difficult spot. NBA NBA If the Nets didn't switch, Pritchard had a clear path to the rim. Instead, Mikel Brown Jr. switched onto Tatum. Brown, listed at 6-foot-4, was giving up six inches to Tatum. Noah Clowney — the 6-foot-10 defender who started the possession guarding Tatum — was much better equipped to defend Boston's star. We know the Nets didn't actually want to switch. Brown admitted as much postgame . Mazzulla made Brown's job even tougher by having Hauser and George move around, keeping their defenders from helping on Tatum. Sure enough, neither Michael Porter Jr. nor Day'Ron Sharpe left their assignments to help on Tatum. NBA The result? The hottest player in the game got one of the cleanest looks you'll see on a final possession. NBA Mazzulla explained after the game that the final possession was a read designed to put Tatum and Pritchard in a two-on-two situation. "JT got the switch; he held him underneath and then created separation, caught it and drove away from help. And he was able to knock it down and win the game for us," Mazzulla said. The Nets made their choice. Tatum made them pay. More Celtics Latest Celtics news TD Garden fan guide: What to know before you go Complete history of Celtics championships

item.title: Real Madrid issue official apology to China following Kylian Mbappe's controversial Mao Zedong 'dictator' comments
item.description: Real Madrid C.F. v RB Leipzig - UEFA Champions League 2026/27 League Phase MD3 - Getty Images Sport Real Madrid have been forced to issue a formal public apology to the people of China following a significant backlash against Kylian Mbappe. The French superstar landed himself in hot water after making comments that were widely perceived as disrespectful toward the nation's founding leader. Mbappe meme sparks severe commercial backlash During an online interview, Mbappe referenced a meme depicting himself as Mao Zedong. The France striker referred to the founding leader of Communist China as a "Chinese dictator", which immediately triggered widespread outrage across the nation. The commercial fallout was swift and severe. The forward lost lucrative brand deals with at least three different Chinese companies , including Dongpeng Beverage, Mengniu, and Milkground. Furthermore, the China Media Group (CMG) took major action by suspending broadcasts of La Liga fixtures and any matches featuring the player. The state broadcaster subsequently demanded formal apologies from the striker, Real Madrid, and the Spanish top flight, according to Associated Press . Real Madrid and Mbappe express deep regret Facing mounting pressure, Mbappe released a statement on Tuesday acknowledging his mistake . The attacker admitted his remarks were "ill-judged" and stated: "I now understand that it hurt many people in China and in Chinese communities." On Wednesday, Real Madrid followed suit with a comprehensive official statement to repair the damaged relationship. "Real Madrid C.F. wishes to express its apologies to the Chinese people for any distress that may have been caused by the recent remarks made by our player, Kylian Mbappe," the club said. "Our club holds deep respect for China, its history, its culture, and its citizens, as well as for the millions of Chinese fans who feel affection and admiration for Real Madrid. "The club joins the public apology expressed by Kylian Mbappe, in which the player himself has conveyed his regret for his words and reiterated his respect for the Chinese people. "Real Madrid reaffirms its commitment to the values of respect, coexistence, and cross-cultural understanding, and expresses its desire to continue strengthening the bonds of friendship and affection that unite it with China and its citizens." Broadcasting standoff remains unresolved The rapid interventions from all parties highlight the immense importance of the Chinese market to European football. In addition to player and club statements, La Liga have also formally apologised to mitigate the fallout. CMG confirmed they have received Real Madrid's formal apology. Rebuilding bridges in the Asian market Associated Press report added that China's Foreign Ministry confirmed on Wednesday that they are taking Mbappe's apology "seriously", though the long-term impact on his personal brand remains entirely uncertain. It is still unclear whether the forward can recover his terminate

item.title: Survey shows how Americans really feel about Enes Kanter declaring for WNBA
item.description: Photo by Michael Reaves/Getty Images Declaring for the WNBA got Kanter Freedom the attention he wanted, but fans aren’t totally on his side. Enes Kanter just won’t let this WNBA thing die. Ever since claiming he wanted in on the league, he’s turned it into a full-blown media tour, jumping on every podcast, cable news hit, and radio show. But things got properly messy when he took the stunt straight to the arena. Showing up courtside at the WNBA finals ended with security stepping in and hauling him right out of the building. What started as an online headline has turned into an awkward, dragged-out spectacle that’s wearing thin on just about everyone. Americans aren’t buying Enes Kanter’s WNBA stunt A recent YouGov survey conducted with The Bulwark and Pablo Torre Finds Out revealed that Enes Kanter’s self-declared WNBA campaign largely backfired with the American public. Polling 1,417 U.S. adults about Freedom’s move to protest transgender-inclusion policies by claiming eligibility for the women’s league, the numbers show clear pushback. Nearly half of respondents, 47%, disapproved of his actions, with a whopping 36% strongly disapproving. By contrast, only 30% approved overall, evenly split at 15% each for strongly and somewhat approving. Another 23% remained unsure, but the takeaway is obvious, while the outspoken former NBA big man definitely succeeded at stirring the pot, his stunt failed to rally mainstream sports fans to his corner. Read more: ‘A mess’ – WNBA fans are split after Atlanta Dream’s letter to fans over Finals’ Game 6 arena issues Poll shows who Americans truly prefer out of Caitlin Clark and Angel Reese NBA legend Tracy McGrady offers simple solution to WNBA Game 6 scheduling problem

item.title: Carrick and Fernandes hold clear-the-air talks before Chelsea trip
item.description: FILE PHOTO - Manchester United head coach Michael Carrick instructs Bruno Fernandes on the touchline during the English Premier League soccer match between Manchester United and Manchester City at Old Trafford. (is associated with: «Carrick and Fernandes hold clear-the-air talks before Chelsea trip») Martin Rickett/PA Wire/dpa Manchester United head coach Michael Carrick and captain Bruno Fernandes have held clear-the-air talks. The Press Association understands Carrick and Fernandes met at United’s Carrington training ground for talks that were separate to a wider meeting of the full squad to discuss a way forward from their current predicament. Fernandes appeared to question Carrick’s tactics in the wake of last week’s 4-1 Champions League loss to Como, and was dropped for Sunday’s Premier League match at home to Bournemouth, remaining on the bench throughout as United fell to stunning 3-0 loss that piled the pressure on Carrick. However, after the talks, Fernandes is now considered available for the crunch match away to Chelsea on Saturday. Fernandes, who lately has looked a shadow of the player of who was named the PFA Players’ player of the year last term, is described as being back to the best version of himself over the past 48 hours following a difficult period on and off the pitch. Sunday’s result left United down in 16th place in the Premier League with only one league win – over newly-promoted Ipswich – this term. Many observers had expected the axe to fall on the boss in the wake of Sunday’s defeat, but Carrick took training on Tuesday with the club resolving to give the 45-year-old more time to turn things around. Fernandes was the second player to make outspoken comments in a post-match interview in the space of two weeks, with Lisandro Martínez having taken aim at the club’s hierarchy in an explosive interview following the 2-0 Champions League loss to Atlético Madrid on October 13. Carrick took charge of the team in January, stabilizing the club after Ruben Amorim’s often turbulent reign, overseeing an excellent run of results which culminated in a third-placed finish and a return to the Champions League. The popular former United midfielder was rewarded with a two-year deal in the summer, but just five months after signing it he has come under major scrutiny with United having won only two of their 12 matches in all competitions, those against Ipswich and Champions League minnows Sabah. But while Carrick’s position in the dugout means he faces much of the scrutiny, Martinez’s comments in Madrid focused higher up the chain of command. Director of football Jason Wilcox and chief executive Omar Berrada are also under the microscope after what is seen as a failure to properly strengthen the squad in the summer, when United put all their focus on midfield reinforcements but failed to sign either a left-back or a striker. item.title: Sturgis girls, Centreville boys claim St. Joe County team titles
item.description: STURGIS — The Centreville boys and Sturgis girls ran away with victories Monday afternoon, Oct. 26. The two were crowned team champions at the St. Joseph County cross country invitational. Sturgis had the county champion in Alice Starkey, who ran a time of 20:47 to lead the field. The Trojans scored 27 points to win the championship while Three Rivers was second as a team with 39. The Centreville boys were led by Will Hulin. The Bulldogs scored 25 team points, finishing ahead of Three Rivers, which scored 41. VOTE VOTE VOTE: Cast your votes for the Footballer of the Week, presented by Glen Oaks CC! Nick Overweg ran to third place at 16:41, and Max Reed finished fourth at 17:08 while Will Swanwick came in fifth position with a time of 17:38. Tanner Bingaman came in 12th place for the Bulldogs at 18:40. Three Rivers was second as a team on Monday with 41 points; Sturgis finished third with 79. White Pigeon came in fourth (112), Constantine was fifth (137) and Colon finished sixth (172). The Wildcats were led by David Kore. He finished second overall in the race at 16:34. Elijah Harris (seventh, 18:12), Tony Hilton (ninth, 18:27) and Bryce Robinson (10th, 18:33) each finished inside the Top 10 as well. Cesar Rodriguez Delgado was 13th with a time of 18:48. Sturgis was led by Milo Barry, who finished sixth with a time of 17:54. Cooper Hohn came in 11th position at 18:39, and Niko Morales was 21st at 19:21. Caleb Hohn finished 24th at 19:57, and Henry Ebert ran a time of 20:07 to finish 25th. Leading White Pigeon was Aiden Jackson in 14th position at 18:55. Derek Sonnevil came in 40th at 21:15, Brock Warren was 48th at 22:10, Quinn Maxwell came in 55th at 23:04 and Frank Cantanzarite was 56th at 23:32. Dylan Smith came in 46th at 22:04, Adam Trevino was 58th at 23:52, Kane Bernheisel ran to 61st at 24:32 and Sebastian Hernandez was 65th at 28:29. After Starkey, Sturgis got a fourth-place finish from Emmy Farber (21:32) and a fifth-place finish from Ally Farber (21:35). Zak Wiley was 22nd at 19:29, Isaac Doubblestein finished 34th at 20:41, William Throw was 35th at 20:41 and Matthew McGahan came in 37th at 20:49. Aaron Hofmeister led Constantine, finishing eighth at 18:13. Derek Sonnevil came in 40th at 21:15, Brock Warren was 48th at 22:10, Quinn Maxwell came in 55th at 23:04 and Frank Cantanzarite was 56th at 23:32. Colon got a 41st-place finish from Charlie Wielenga, whose time was 21:15. Dylan Smith came in 46th at 22:04, Adam Trevino was 58th at 23:52, Kane Bernheisel ran to 61st at 24:32 and Sebastian Hernandez was 65th at 28:29. After Starkey, Sturgis got a fourth-place finish from Emmy Farber (21:32) and a fifth-place finish from Ally Farber (21:35). Annmarie Taylor finished sixth overall at 21:39, Olivia Green came in 11th position at 22:24 and Eleanor Park was 14th at 22:47. Three Rivers finished with three runners in the Top 10. Kloey Osborn came in second place at 21:17, and Lillie Kerr was third at 21:26. Lauren Kane ran a time of 21:46 for seventh. Brynn Copenhaver ran to 12th place at 22:39, and Simone Allen came in 16th at 22:58. Constantine had a pair of runners in the Top 10. Allison Burns was eighth overall at 21:51, and Anna Davidhizar came in ninth at 22:04. Paytin Featherstone ran to 17th at 23:12, Eden Huser Company was 20th at 23:37 and Sofia Avila came in 29th at 25:34. Emily Falkenstein was 10th to lead Centreville at 22:11. Addison Johnson acme in 13th at 22:41, and Norah Lammon was 18th at 23:13. Hazel Sloat finished 19th at 23:15, and Katelyn Trattles came in 24th at 24:37. The All-County team for the girls was Starkey, Osborn, Kerr, Farber, Farber, Taylor, Kane, Burns, Davidhizar, Falkenstein, Green, Copenhaver, Johnson, Park and Aubrey Miller of White Pigeon. The all-county team for the boys was Hulin, Kore, Overweg, Reed, Swanwick, Barry, Harris, Hofmeister, Hilton, Robinson, Hohn, Bingaman, Rodriguez Delgado, Jackson and Mason Wolfe of Three Rivers.
